en: A powerful and addictive drug derived from opium producing intense euphoria, classed as an illegal narcotic in most of the world.

heroin.ety: Since the 1890s, by genericization from German Heroin, originally a trademark, from Ancient Greek ἥρως (hḗrōs, “hero”) and the suffix -in (“-ine”). Said to have been called thus to evoke quick and sweeping effect as a painkiller and cough suppressant (its original uses). Alternatively explained as a reference to the heroic school of medicine.

ex.en: She admitted to having heroin.
ex.ja: 彼女はヘロインを持っていることを認めた。

ex.en: He is a heroin addict.
ex.ja: 彼はヘロインの常習者だ。

ex.en: Tom is a heroin addict.
ex.ja: トムはヘロイン中毒だ。

note.ja: ドイツの商標名 Heroin から。hero（英雄）+ -in。飲むと英雄になったような気分になるとされたことから。

en: The act of illustrating; the act of making clear and distinct.
The state of being illustrated, or of being made clear and distinct.

illustration.ety: Borrowed from Middle French illustration, from Latin illūstrātiō, from illūstrō (“to illustrate”). By surface analysis, illustrate + -ion.

ex.en: An illustration may make the point clear.
ex.ja: 一例をあげればその点ははっきりするだろう。

ex.en: This book has 252 pages exclusive of illustrations.
ex.ja: この本は挿絵を除いて２５２ページある。

ex.en: Here's an illustration at the top of this page.
ex.ja: このページの上に挿し絵が有ります。

note.ja: illustrate（説明する）+ -ation。in + lustrare（照らす）。「光を当てて明らかにする」→「挿絵・実例」。luster（光沢）と同じ。

en: A pointer or index that indicates something.
A meter or gauge.

indicator.ety: From Late Latin indicātor (“one who points out”), from Latin indicō (“point out”). By surface analysis, indicate + -or; see indicate.

note.ja: indicate（示す）+ -or。「指標・表示器」→ 車の「方向指示器」。

en: A condition or state (of social, cultural, or legal matters) that is not equal; especially, such a condition that is thereby also unfair.
A statement that of two quantities one is specifically less than (or greater than) another. Symbol: < or ≤ or > or ≥ or ne , as appropriate.

inequality.ety:
From Middle English inequalite, from Old French inequalité, from Medieval Latin inaequālitās, from Latin inaequālis (“unequal”), from in- (“not”) + aequālis (“equal”).
Morphologically inequal + -ity and in- + equality.

ex.en: I never denied the presence of inequality.
ex.ja: 不公平の存在は否認しなかった。

ex.en: No inequality should be allowed to exist between men and women.
ex.ja: 男女間に不均等が存在することは許されるべきではない。

note.ja: in（否定）+ equ（等しい）+ al + ity。等しくないこと →「不平等・格差」。

en: To decode the meaning of a topic and then act, whether to continue researching the topic, follow through, act in opposition, or further t…
To explain or tell the meaning of; to translate orally into intelligible or familiar language or terms. applied especially to language, b…

interpret.ety: From Middle English interpreten, from Old French enterpreter, (French interpréter), from Latin interpretor (“to explain, expound, interpret”), past participle interpretatus, from interpres (“an agent, broker, explainer, interpreter, negotiator”), from inter (“between”) + -pres, probably the root of pretium (“price”); -pres is probably connected with Ancient Greek φράζειν (phrázein, “to point out, show, explain, declare, speak”), from which φραδή (phradḗ, “understanding”), φράσις (phrásis, “speech”); see phrase.

ex.en: I don't know how to interpret his words.
ex.ja: 彼の言葉をどう解釈していいのか分からない。

ex.en: This sentence can be interpreted in two ways.
ex.ja: この文は二通りに解釈することができる。

ex.en: This sentence may be interpreted another way.
ex.ja: この文はもう一つの解釈ができる。

note.ja: ラテン語 interpres（仲介者・通訳）から。inter（間）+ pret（値段）とされる。「間に立って取り次ぐ」→「解釈する・通訳する」。

en: Freedom provided by the cessation of activities.
Free time, time free from work or duties.

leisure.ety: From Middle English leyser, from Anglo-Norman leisir, variant of Old French loisir (“to enjoy oneself”) (Modern French loisir survives as a noun), substantive use of a verb, from Latin licēre (“be permitted”). Displaced native Old English ǣmetta.

ex.en: Please look through these papers at your leisure.
ex.ja: あなたが暇な時にこの書類に目を通してください。

ex.en: You can do it at your leisure.
ex.ja: それは暇なときにすればよろしい。

ex.en: A friend to everybody is a friend to leisure.
ex.ja: すべての人の友は誰の友でもない。

note.ja: 古フランス語 leisir（許されている）から。ラテン語 licere（許される）。license と同じ。「好きにしてよい時間」→「余暇」。

en: To allow to be used by someone temporarily, on condition that it or its equivalent will be returned.
To make a loan.

lend.ety:
From earlier len (with excrescent -d, as in sound), from Middle English lenen, lænen, from Old English lǣnan (“to lend; give, grant, lease”), from Proto-West Germanic *laihnijan, from Proto-Germanic *laihnijaną (“to loan”), from Proto-Germanic *laihną (“loan”), from Proto-Indo-European *leykʷ- (“to leave, leave over”).
Cognate with Scots len, lend (“to lend”), West Frisian liene (“to lend, borrow, loan”), Dutch lenen (“to lend, borrow, loan”), Danish låne (“to lend, loan”), Swedish låna (“to lend, loan”), Icelandic lána (“to lend, loan”), Icelandic léna (“to grant”), Latin linquō (“quit, leave

ex.en: I will lend you whatever book you need.
ex.ja: 君が必要な本は何でもお貸ししましょう。

ex.en: Lend me some money if you have any.
ex.ja: 金を持っていたらいくらか貸して下さい。

ex.en: Lend me something with which to cut this.
ex.ja: 何かこれを切るものを貸してください。

note.ja: 古英語 lǣnan（貸す）から。loan（ローン・貸付）と同じ祖先。

en: To relax; to spend time lazily; to stand, sit, or recline, in an indolent manner.
To walk or go in a leisurely manner.
The act of someone who lounges; idle reclining.
A room of a house for casual relaxing and entertaining.

lounge.ety: Origin uncertain. Perhaps borrowed from French s'allonger (“to lie down”). Compare French longer (“to walk along”). Compare also German lungern (“to hang or lounge around, linger”).

ex.en: Let's drop in at that coffee lounge.
ex.ja: ちょっとあの喫茶店に立ち寄ろう。

ex.en: We ate a quick lunch in a coffee lounge.
ex.ja: 私達は喫茶店で素早い昼食を食べた。

ex.en: We ate lunch in a coffee lounge.
ex.ja: 私たちは喫茶店で昼食を食べた。

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。「ぶらぶらする」→「くつろぐ場所」→「ラウンジ」。

en: In a lucky manner; by good fortune; fortunately.

luckily.ety:
Etymology tree
English lucky
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English luckily
From lucky + -ly.

ex.en: Luckily, he was on time for the train.
ex.ja: 運良く彼は汽車に間に合った。

ex.en: Luckily he had enough money to pay the bill.
ex.ja: 運良く彼はその請求書の支払いができるだけのお金を持ち合わせていた。

ex.en: Luckily, I was able to get the tickets yesterday.
ex.ja: 幸運にも、昨日切符を手に入れることができた。

note.ja: luck（運）+ -ily。「運よく」。

en: Handwritten, or by extension manually typewritten, as opposed to being mechanically reproduced.
A book, composition or any other document, written by hand (or manually typewritten), not mechanically reproduced.
A single, original copy of a book, article, composition etc, written by hand or even printed, submitted as original for (copy-editing and…

manuscript.ety: 1597, from Medieval Latin manūscrīptus, a calque of Germanic origin, equivalent to Latin manū (ablative of manus (“hand”)) + Latin scrīptus (past participle of scribere (“to write”)). Not found in Classical Latin.

ex.en: The manuscript had been written out by hand.
ex.ja: その原稿は手で清書されていた。

ex.en: I've been writing this manuscript for a year.
ex.ja: 私はこの一年原稿を書いている。

ex.en: Can you manage to complete the manuscript by Friday?
ex.ja: 金曜日までに何とか原稿を仕上げられますか。

note.ja: manu（手）+ script（書かれた）。手で書かれたもの →「原稿・写本」。

en: A building or institution where money (originally, only coins) is produced under government licence.
A vast sum of money; (by extension) a large amount of something.
To reproduce (coins), usually en masse, under licence.
To invent; to forge; to fabricate; to fashion.
In near-perfect condition; uncirculated.
Unused with original gum; as issued originally.

mint.ety: From Middle English mynt, münet (“money, coin”), from Old English mynet (“coin”), from late Proto-West Germanic *munit, from Latin monēta (“place for making coins, coined money”), from the temple of Juno Moneta (named for Monēta mother of the Muses), where coins were made. Doublet of money and manat. The verb is from the noun; Old English mynetian (“to mint”) is a parallel formation.

ex.en: Would you like a mint?
ex.ja: ハッカ飴、一つどう？

ex.en: I don't like mint tea.
ex.ja: ミントティーは、苦手なのよ。

ex.en: John works at the mint.
ex.ja: ジョンは造幣局で働いています。

note.ja: 「ハッカ」はギリシャ語 minthē から。「造幣局」はラテン語 moneta（女神ユノの神殿・造幣所）からで別語。money と同じ語源。

en: The smallest particle of a specific element or compound that retains the chemical properties of that element or compound; two or more ato…
A tiny amount.

molecule.ety:
Etymology tree
Latin mōlēs
Proto-Indo-European *-lós
Proto-Indo-European *-elós
Proto-Italic *-elos
Proto-Italic *-kelos
Latin -cula
New Latin mōlēculalbor.
French moléculebor.
English molecule
Borrowed from French molécule, from New Latin molecula (“a molecule”), diminutive of Latin moles (“a mass”).

ex.en: Organic matter is formed by large molecules.
ex.ja: 有機物というのは大きな分子から形成されている。

ex.en: A water molecule has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
ex.ja: 水分子は、２個の水素原子と１個の酸素原子からなる。

ex.en: A molecule of water is made up of one oxygen and two hydrogen atoms.
ex.ja: 水分子は一個の酸素原子と二個の水素原子から出来ています。

note.ja: フランス語 molécule から。ラテン語 moles（かたまり）+ 縮小。「小さなかたまり」→「分子」。

en: The act of notifying.
A specific piece of information that serves to notify.

notification.ety: From Middle French notification, from Old French notificacion, from Latin nōtificātiō.

ex.en: Wasn't there a notification from the app?
ex.ja: アプリから通知きてなかった？

ex.en: Kyoko has mail notifications turned off and last updated on the 25th January 2016.
ex.ja: 京子さんはメール通知OFFで最終更新日時2016年1月25日です。

note.ja: notify（知らせる）+ -ication。ラテン語 notus（知られた）+ facere（する）。「知らせること」→「通知」。notice と同じ。

en: Any sudden brightening of a previously inconspicuous star.

nova.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *nu
Proto-Indo-European *néwos
Proto-Italic *nowos
Latin novusder.
English nova
Feminine nominative singular of Latin novus (“new”). The feminine is used since stella (“star”) is feminine; thus nova is a shortening of new star (“nova stella”), first used in this sense in 1573 by Tycho Brahe.

note.ja: ラテン語 nova（新しい）から。nov（新しい）。新しく現れたように見える星 →「新星」。

en: A line marking the boundary of an object figure.
The outer shape of an object or figure.
To draw an outline of; to describe.
To summarize.

ex.en: I gave him an outline of the incident.
ex.ja: 僕は彼に事件のいきさつを一通り話した。

ex.en: He gave me a brief outline of the plan.
ex.ja: 彼は計画の骨組みを簡単に説明してくれた。

ex.en: First, I'm going to do an outline of my new website.
ex.ja: まず新しいサイトの概説をしようと思う。

note.ja: out（外）+ line（線）。「外側の線」→「輪郭・概要」。

en: Dough made from wheat and water and sometimes mixed with egg and formed into various shapes; often sold in dried form and typically boile…
Any type of noodle.

pasta.ety:
Etymology tree
Ancient Greek πάσσω (pássō)
Proto-Indo-European *-tós
Proto-Hellenic *-tós
Ancient Greek -τός (-tós)
Ancient Greek παστός (pastós)
Ancient Greek παστά (pastá)bor.
Late Latin pasta
Italian pastabor.
English pasta
Borrowed from Italian pasta (“paste; pasta, noodles”), from Late Latin pasta (“dough, pastry cake, paste”), from Ancient Greek παστά (pastá, “barley porridge”), neuter plural of παστός (pastós, “sprinkled with salt”), from Ancient Greek πάσσω (pássō, “to sprinkle”). Doublet of paste.

ex.en: It's been a while since I've had pasta.
ex.ja: パスタを食べるのは久しぶりだな。

ex.en: Can you keep an eye on the pasta?
ex.ja: パスタを見ててくれる？

ex.en: The pasta here's pretty good. And the pizza too.
ex.ja: ここ、結構パスタがいけるのよ。あとピザも。

note.ja: イタリア語 pasta（練り物）から。paste（ペースト）と同じ。

en: The sixteenth letter of the Classical and Modern Greek alphabets and the seventeenth in Old Greek.
An irrational and transcendental constant representing the ratio of the circumference of a Euclidean circle to its diameter; approximatel…
To spill or mix printing type.
Not part of the usual font character set; especially, non-Roman type or symbols as opposed to standard alphanumeric Roman type.

pi.ety: From Koine Greek πῖ (pî), from Ancient Greek πεῖ (peî), ultimately from Proto-Semitic *pay- (“mouth”). Doublet of pe. Its mathematical use apparently stems from its use as the first letter in περιφέρεια (periphéreia, “periphery; circumference”) and was first cited in 1706 in the Synopsis Palmariorum Matheseos by William Jones.

ex.en: I went to buy a piñata of my favorite anime character.
ex.ja: 僕は好きなアニメキャラのピニャータを買いに行ったんだ。

ex.en: I want to go buy a piñata of my favorite anime character.
ex.ja: 私は好きなアニメキャラのピニャータを買いに行きたい。

ex.en: I bought a soap in France that smells like piña colada.
ex.ja: フランスでピニャコラーダの香りがする石鹸を買ったんだ。

note.ja: ギリシャ文字 π。円周（perimetros）の頭文字から。

en: Well-mannered, civilized.

polite.ety: From Latin polītus (“polished”), past participle of poliō (“to polish, smooth”); see polish.

ex.en: We treated him in the politest manner possible.
ex.ja: 私達はできる限りの丁寧な態度で彼を取り扱った。

ex.en: It is polite to open doors for people.
ex.ja: 人のためにドアを開けてあげるのは礼儀正しい。

ex.en: It is not polite to point at others.
ex.ja: 他人を指差すのは失礼なことです。

note.ja: ラテン語 politus（磨かれた）から。磨き上げられた →「礼儀正しい・洗練された」。※ polis（都市）とは別語源。

en: The act of receiving, or the fact of having been received.
A quantity or amount received; takings.
To give or write a receipt (for something).
To put a receipt on, as by writing or stamping; to mark a bill as having been paid.

receipt.ety: From Middle English receyt, recorded since c. 1386 as "statement of ingredients in a potion or medicine," from Anglo-Norman or Old Northern French receite (“receipt, recipe”) (1304), altered (by influence of receit (“he receives”), from Latin recipit) from Old French recete, from Latin receptus, perfect passive participle of recipiō, itself from re- (“back”) + capiō (“to take”). The unpronounced p was later inserted to make the word appear closer to its Latin root. Doublet of recept and recipe. False cognate of Persian رسید (resid) (whence Urdu رسید (rasīd)).

ex.en: We need the receipt signed by Mr. Smith.
ex.ja: 私たちはスミスさんがサインした領収書が必要です。

ex.en: We need the receipt that Mr. Smith signed.
ex.ja: 私たちはスミスさんがサインした領収書が必要です。

ex.en: I am in receipt of your letter.
ex.ja: お手紙落手いたしました。

note.ja: re（元へ）+ ceipt（取る）。受け取ったこと →「領収書・受領」。receive と同じ cap。

en: The quality of being reliable, dependable, or trustworthy.
the ability to measure the same thing consistently (of a measurement indicating the degree to which the measure is consistent); that is, …

reliability.ety:
Etymology tree
English rely
Proto-Indo-European *-dʰlom
Proto-Italic *-ðlom
Proto-Italic *-ðlis
Latin -bilis
Latin -ābilis
Old French -ablebor.
Middle English -able
English -able
English reliable
Proto-Indo-European *-teh₂
Proto-Indo-European *-ts
Proto-Indo-European *-teh₂tsder.
Latin -itās
Old French -itebor.
Middle English -ite
English -ity
English reliability
From reliable + -ity.

ex.en: All he has going for him is his reliability.
ex.ja: 誠実さだけが彼の取り柄だね。

ex.en: He has a good name for reliability.
ex.ja: 彼は信頼できるという評判だ。

ex.en: I can assure you of his reliability.
ex.ja: 彼が信頼できることは君に保証できる。

note.ja: reliable（信頼できる）+ -ity。「信頼性」。

en: A retail sales company or salesman.

retailer.ety:
Etymology tree
English retail

Proto-Indo-European *-os?

Proto-Indo-European *-eh₂so-

From retail + -er.

note.ja: retail（小売り）+ -er。re（再び）+ tailler（切る）。「細かく切り分けて売る」→「小売り」。tailor（仕立て屋：布を切る人）も同じ。

ja: （ファッションショーの）ランウェイ

en: A defined, narrow section of land or an artificial structure used for access.
The usual path taken by deer or other wild animals, such as from a forest to a water source.

runway.ety:
Etymology tree
English run
Proto-Indo-European *weǵʰ-der.
Proto-Germanic *wegaz
Proto-West Germanic *weg
Old English weġ
Middle English wey
English way
English runway
From run + way.

ex.en: An airplane touched down on the runway.
ex.ja: 飛行機は滑走路に着陸した。

note.ja: run（走る）+ way（道）。「走る道」→「滑走路・ランウェイ」。

en: A three-dimensional work of art created by shaping malleable objects and letting them harden or by chipping away pieces from a rock (scul…
More generally (since modernism), a three-dimensional work of art of any material or of mixed materials, whether sculpted, assembled, fou…
To fashion something into a three-dimensional figure.
To represent something in sculpture.

sculpture.ety: From Middle English sculpture, from Old French sculpture, from Latin sculptūra (“sculpture”), from sculpō (“to cut out, to carve in stone”).

ex.en: They have taken the form of sculptures.
ex.ja: それらは彫刻の形を取ってきた。

ex.en: The city holds an ice sculpture festival each year.
ex.ja: 街では毎年、氷彫刻の祭典が開催されます。

ex.en: The sculptures are of great value.
ex.ja: その彫刻は非常に貴重である。

note.ja: ラテン語 sculpere（彫る）から。「彫ったもの」→「彫刻」。

en: A case for displaying merchandise or valuable items.
A setting, occasion, or medium for exhibiting something or someone, especially in an attractive or favorable aspect.
To display, demonstrate, show, or present.

note.ja: show（見せる）+ case（ケース）。「見せるための箱」→「ショーケース・披露の場」。

en: Auxiliary or supplemental.
Secondary or subordinate.
A company owned by a parent company or a holding company, also called daughter company or sister company.
A subordinate theme.

subsidiary.ety: From Middle French subsidiaire, from Latin subsidiarius (“belonging to a reserve”).

ex.en: The company is our wholly-owned subsidiary.
ex.ja: その会社は我々の１００％子会社である。

ex.en: Overseas subsidiaries are putting out top-of the-line products.
ex.ja: 海外の子会社は最高級品を生産しています。

note.ja: ラテン語 subsidium（予備軍・援助）から。sub（下に）+ sidere（座る）。「後ろに控える」→「補助的な・子会社」。subsidy（補助金）。

en: The ordinal numeral form of ten; next in order after that which is ninth.
Being one of ten equal parts of a whole.
The person or thing coming next after the ninth in a series; that which is in the tenth position.
One of ten equal parts of a whole.
To divide by ten, into tenths.

tenth.ety: From Middle English tenth, tenthe. Old English had tēoþa (origin of Modern English tithe), but the force of analogy to the cardinal number "ten" caused Middle English speakers to recreate the regular ordinal and re-insert the nasal consonant. Ultimately from Proto-Germanic *tehundô. Equivalent to ten (numeral) + -th (suffix forming ordinals).

ex.en: October is the tenth month of the year.
ex.ja: 「１０月」は１年の中で１０回目の月にあたります。

ex.en: Possession is nine-tenths of the law.
ex.ja: 現実の占有は九分の勝ち目。

ex.en: Jack was born on August the tenth.
ex.ja: ジャックは８月１０日に生まれた。

note.ja: ten + -th（序数）。「10番目」。

en: The study of God, a god, or gods; and of the truthfulness of religion in general.
Synonym of religious studies.

theology.ety: From Middle English theologie, from Middle French theologie, from Old French theologie, from Latin theologia, from Koine Greek θεολογία (theología), from θεολόγος (theológos, adjective), from θεός (theós) + λόγος (lógos). By surface analysis, theo- + -logy.

note.ja: the（神）+ o + log（学問）+ y。神の学問 →「神学」。

en: Beneath the surface of the water; of or pertaining to the region beneath the water surface.
Beneath the water line of a vessel.
So as to go beneath the surface of the water.
Underlying water or body of water, for example in an aquifer or the deep ocean.
A type of lure which lies beneath the water surface.
To water or irrigate insufficiently.

ex.en: He was underwater for three minutes.
ex.ja: 彼は３分間水にもぐっていた。

ex.en: Do you have underwater photography equipment?
ex.ja: 水中撮影機材はお持ちですか？

ex.en: Do you have an underwater camera?
ex.ja: 水中カメラって、持ってる？

note.ja: under（下に）+ water。「水中の」。

en: A vector quantity that denotes the rate of change of position with respect to time, combining speed with a directional component.
A rapidity of motion.

velocity.ety: From Middle French vélocité, from Latin vēlōcitās (“speed”), from vēlōx (“fast”), thus a doublet of veloce.

ex.en: The velocity of light is about 186,000 miles per second.
ex.ja: 光の速度は秒速およそ186,000マイルである。

ex.en: Light travels at a velocity of 186,000 miles per second.
ex.ja: 光は秒速186,000マイルで進む。

note.ja: ラテン語 velox（速い）から。「速さ・速度」。

en: Any oily, water-resistant, solid or semisolid substance; normally long-chain hydrocarbons, alcohols or esters.
Beeswax (a wax secreted by bees).
Made of wax.
To coat with wax or a similar material.
To form a wax (a thick maple syrup).

wax.ety:
From Middle English wax, from Old English weax, from Proto-Germanic *wahsą, possibly from Proto-Indo-European *woḱ-so-.

note.ja: ラテン語 cardo（ちょうつがい）から。「物事の要となる」→「基本的な」→ 教会の要職 →「枢機卿」。枢機卿の赤い衣から「緋色」。

en: Buddy, sport, mate. (as a term of address)
To act or behave like a champ; to endure.

champ.ety:

en: A sparkling white wine made from a blend of grapes, especially Chardonnay and pinot, produced in Champagne, France, by the méthode champe…
Any sparkling wine made by the méthode champenoise.
Of a very pale brownish-gold colour, similar to that of champagne.
To ply or treat with champagne.
To drink champagne.

champagne.ety: Borrowed from French champagne (“sparkling wine from the Champagne region”), from Champagne (“region and former province of France”), from Late Latin campānia (in full Campānia Rēmēnsis), from campāneus (“of or pertaining to the fields”), from Latin campus (“level ground; field, plain”), from Proto-Indo-European *kh₂emp- (“to bend, curve”). The English word is a doublet of campagna (“flat stretch of countryside”) (dated), campaign, and campania.

ex.en: Tom doesn't know the difference between wine and champagne.
ex.ja: トムにはワインとシャンパンの違いが分からない。

ex.en: I'll take a glass of champagne.
ex.ja: シャンペンを下さい。

ex.en: Orange juice or champagne?
ex.ja: オレンジジュースにするか、シャンペンにするか。

note.ja: フランスのシャンパーニュ地方の名前から。ラテン語 campania（平野）。campus、camp も同じ。

en: A group of singers and dancers in a theatrical performance or religious festival who commented on the main performance in speech or song.
A song performed by the singers of such a group.
To sing (a song), express (a sentiment), or recite or say (words) in chorus.
To express concurrence with (something said by another person); to echo.

chorus.ety: The noun is borrowed from Medieval Latin chorus (“church choir”), Latin chorus (“group of dancers and singers; dance”), from Ancient Greek χορός (khorós, “group of dancers and singers, choir, chorus; dance accompanied by song; round dance”); The verb is derived from the noun. Doublet of choir, chore, and hora.

ex.en: The party ended up with a chorus.
ex.ja: パーティーは合唱で終わった。

ex.en: We joined in on the chorus.
ex.ja: 私たちは一緒に歌った。

ex.en: They all joined in the chorus.
ex.ja: 彼らはみな一緒にコーラスを歌いました。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 khoros（踊りと歌の一団）から。choir と同じ語源。

en: The state or measure of being clear, either in appearance, thought or style; lucidity.
The ability to be easily understood.

clarity.ety: From Middle English claritee, from Old French clarté, from Latin clāritās, from clārus (“clear”); equivalent to clear + -ity.

ex.en: Those people appreciate clarity.
ex.ja: その人たちは明瞭さをよしとする。

note.ja: clar（明るい・明らかな）+ ity。明らかなこと →「明快さ・透明さ」。clear（澄んだ）。

en: Kept, or meant to be kept, secret within a certain circle of persons; not intended to be known publicly.

confidential.ety: From Latin cōnfīdentia + English -al. Possibly a calque of French confidentiel. First attested in 1641.

ex.en: He soon became confidential with the man.
ex.ja: じきに彼はその男と打ち明けた。

ex.en: Please keep this information confidential.
ex.ja: この情報は内密にしてください。

ex.en: This information is confidential.
ex.ja: この情報は秘密です。

note.ja: con（完全に）+ fid（信頼する）+ ential。信頼の上で打ち明けられた →「機密の・内密の」。

zh: 協調動作的能力 /协调动作的能力

en: The act of coordinating, making different people or things work together for a goal or effect.
The resulting state of working together; cooperation; synchronization.

coordination.ety: From Middle French coordination, from Late Latin coōrdinātiōnem (accusative of coōrdinātiō), from con- + ōrdinātiō. Morphologically coordinate + -ion.

note.ja: co（共に）+ ordin（順序）+ ation。順序を共に整えること →「調整・協調・連携」。

en: The quality of being discreet.
The ability to make wise choices or decisions.

discretion.ety: From Middle English discrecioun, from Old French discretion, from Late Latin discrētiō, from Latin discerno. Equivalent to discreet + -ion.

ex.en: Discretion is proper to judges.
ex.ja: 裁判官には慎重さがなくてはならない。

ex.en: Discretion is the better part of valor.
ex.ja: 用心深さは勇気の大半である。

ex.en: He has attained to years of discretion.
ex.ja: 彼は分別ある年齢に達した。

note.ja: dis（離れて）+ cret（ふるい分ける）+ ion。見分ける力 →「判断の自由・分別・慎重さ」。

en: A trench; a long, shallow indentation, as for irrigation or drainage.
A raised bank of earth and the hedgerow on top.
To discard or abandon; to stop associating with (someone).
To deliberately crash-land an airplane on water.

ditch.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Germanic *dīkaz
Proto-West Germanic *dīk
Old English dīċ
Middle English dich
English ditch
From Middle English dich, from Old English dīċ (“trench, moat”) from Proto-Germanic *dīkaz (compare Swedish dike, Icelandic díki, West Frisian dyk (“dam”), Dutch dijk (“dam”), German Teich (“pond”)), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰeygʷ- (“to stick, set up”) (compare Latin fīgō (“to affix, fasten”), Lithuanian diegti (“to prick; plant”), dýgsti (“to geminate, grow”)). Doublet of dike.

ex.en: I am afraid to jump over the ditch.
ex.ja: 恐くてその溝は跳び越せないよ。

ex.en: I hope you fall in a ditch.
ex.ja: 溝に落ちると希望しています。

ex.en: I'm afraid to jump over the ditch.
ex.ja: 恐くてその溝は跳び越せないよ。

note.ja: 古英語 dīc（溝・土手）から。dike と同じ語源。「溝」→ 溝に捨てる →（口語）「見捨てる」。

en: A structural element resembling the hollow upper half of a sphere.
Anything shaped like an upset bowl, often used as a cover.
To give a domed shape to.

dome.ety: Borrowed from Middle French dome, domme (modern French dôme), from Italian duomo, from Latin domus (ecclesiae) (literally “house (of the church)”), a calque of Ancient Greek οἶκος τῆς ἐκκλησίας (oîkos tês ekklēsías). Doublet of domus and duomo.

ex.en: Have you ever been to the Tokyo Dome?
ex.ja: 東京ドームへ行ったことがありますか？

ex.en: What's the number for the Tokyo Dome?
ex.ja: 東京ドームの電話番号は何番ですか。

note.ja: ラテン語 domus（家）から。（神の家の）丸屋根 →「ドーム・丸屋根」。

en: Any viscous liquid or paste, such as a lubricant, used in preparing a surface.
An absorbent material used to hold a liquid.
To treat with dope (lubricant, etc.).
To add a dopant such as arsenic to (a pure semiconductor such as silicon).

dope.ety:
From Dutch doop (“thick dipping sauce”), from Dutch dopen (“to dip”), from Middle Dutch dopen, from Old Dutch *dōpen, from Frankish *daupijan, from Proto-Germanic *daupijaną.
“Doop” in the sense “narcotic drug” ultimately refers to viscous opium juice, the drug of choice of the ancient Greeks; “insider information” perhaps from knowing which horse had been doped in a race. Sense of "stupid person" perhaps following from the drug sense (i.e. relating to those intoxicated on opium), compare dope up. Related to English dip and German taufen. Unrelated to dopamine.

ex.en: Are you on dope?
ex.ja: 麻薬をやってるの？

note.ja: オランダ語 doop（ソース・浸す液）から。「濃い液体」→「麻薬」。

en: A period of unusually low rainfall, longer and more severe than a dry spell.
A longer than expected term without success, particularly in sport.

drought.ety: From Middle English droughte, droghte, drouȝte, from Old English drūgaþ. Cognate with Dutch droogte, Low German Dröögde. By surface analysis, dry + -t (abstract nominal suffix).

ex.en: Many trees died during the long drought.
ex.ja: 長い干ばつの間に多くの樹が枯れた。

ex.en: If it doesn't rain soon, there will be a drought.
ex.ja: 今すぐに雨が降らないと、干ばつになります。

ex.en: However, during times of drought, lake levels can drop significantly.
ex.ja: ただし、干ばつの時期には湖の水位が大幅に低くなる可能性があります。

note.ja: 古英語 drūgath（乾き）から。dry と同じ祖先。gh は発音しない。

The condition of being or feeling elevated; heightened; exaltation.

en: Assessment, estimation, or regard; especially; favourable estimation or regard.
To set a high value on; to regard with respect or reverence.
To regard something as valuable; to prize.

esteem.ety:
First at end of 16th century; borrowed from Middle French estimer, borrowed from Latin aestimō.
See estimate and aim, an older word, partly a doublet.

ex.en: I esteem it an honor to address this audience.
ex.ja: 皆様にお話出来ることを光栄に存じます。

ex.en: I have a great esteem for you.
ex.ja: あなたにはとても頭が上がりません。

ex.en: I have no self-esteem.
ex.ja: 自分に価値を見いだせない。

note.ja: ラテン語 aestimare（値をつける）から。estimate（見積もる）と同じ語源。「高く値をつける」→「尊敬する」。

en: A thick cloud that forms near the ground; the obscurity of such a cloud.
A mist or film clouding a surface.
To become covered with or as if with fog.
To become obscured in condensation or water.

fog.ety: Origin uncertain; but probably of North Germanic origin. Probably either a back-formation from foggy (“covered with tall grass; thick, marshy”), from the earlier-attested fog (“tall grass”) (see below), or from or related to Danish fog (“spray, shower, drift, storm”), related to Icelandic fok (“spray, any light thing tossed by the wind, snowdrift”), Icelandic fjúka (“to blow, drive”), from Proto-Germanic *feukaną (“to whisk, blow”), from Proto-Indo-European *pug- (“billow, bulge, drift”), from *pew-, *pow- (“to blow, drift, billow”), in which case related to German fauchen (“to hiss, spit, spr

ex.en: The airport was closed because of the fog.
ex.ja: 空港は霧のために閉鎖された。

ex.en: London is no longer a city of fog.
ex.ja: ロンドンはもはや霧の都ではない。

ex.en: I hope the fog will go away soon.
ex.ja: 霧がすぐに晴れてくれればいいんだが。

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。北欧語 fok（吹き寄せる雪）と関係するとされる。

en: A motion of the limbs or body, especially one made to emphasize speech.
An act or a remark that serves as a formality or as a sign of attitude.
To make a gesture or gestures.
To express (something) by a gesture or gestures.

gesture.ety: From Medieval Latin gestūra (“a mode of action”), from Latin gerō (“to bear; (reflexive) bear oneself, behave, act”), past participle gestus. By surface analysis, Latin gest- + -ure.

ex.en: He tried to speak by word or gesture.
ex.ja: 彼は言葉とか手招きで話そうとした。

ex.en: Are these gestures used in the USA?
ex.ja: これらの身振りはアメリカで使われていますか。

ex.en: This gesture is familiar to young people.
ex.ja: この身振りは若い人たちにはよく知られている。

note.ja: ラテン語 gestus（振る舞い）から。gest（運ぶ・行う）+ ure。体の運び方 →「身ぶり・意思表示」。

ja: グリフィン（伝説の生き物）

en: A mythical creature with the body of a lion and head and wings of an eagle.
A griffon vulture, a large vulture (Gyps fulvus) found in the mountainous parts of Southern Europe, North Africa, and Asia Minor, suppose…

griffin.ety: From Middle English griffoun, from Old French griffon, from Late Latin grȳphus, from Classical Latin grȳps, from Ancient Greek γρῡ́ψ (grū́ps).

note.ja: ギリシャ語 grups（曲がったくちばし）から。ワシの頭とライオンの体を持つ伝説の生き物。

en: A writer of history.
One who studies or researches history.

historian.ety: From Middle English historian, historien, from Old French historien, from Latin historia (“story, history”), equivalent to histor(y) + -ian. More at history.

ex.en: He's a historian. He's now studying the structure of war.
ex.ja: 彼は歴史学者だ。今は戦争の構造を研究している。

ex.en: I am a historian.
ex.ja: 私は歴史家です。

ex.en: Professor Suzuki is an expert historian.
ex.ja: 鈴木先生は歴史の専門家です。

note.ja: history（歴史）+ -ian。ギリシャ語 historia（調べて知ること）から。story も同じ語源。

en: Perpendicular to the vertical; parallel to the plane of the horizon; level, flat.
Relating to horizontal markets
A horizontal component of a structure.
Horizon.

horizontal.ety: Borrowed from Middle French horizontal, from horizon, horizonte, from Latin horizōn (stem horizont-).

ex.en: Can you do a horizontal bar back-hip circle?
ex.ja: 逆上がりって、できる？

ex.en: Can you do a horizontal bar forward upward circle?
ex.ja: 逆上がりって、できる？

note.ja: horizon（地平線）+ -al。ギリシャ語 horizein（区切る）。「地平線と平行な」→「水平な」。

en: The act or service of welcoming, receiving, hosting, or entertaining guests; an appropriate attitude of openness, respect, and generosity…
The business of providing catering, lodging and entertainment service; the industry which includes the operation of hotels, restaurants, …

hospitality.ety: From Middle English hospitalite, from Old French hospitalité (modern French hospitalité), from Latin hospitālitās (“hospitality”), from hospitālis (“hospitable”), from hospes (“guest", "host”). Displaced native Old English cumlīþnes (literally “guest gentleness”).

ex.en: Thank you very much for your hospitality today.
ex.ja: 今日はいろいろとありがとうございました。

ex.en: Thank you very much for your hospitality.
ex.ja: お邪魔しました。

ex.en: I cannot thank you too much for your hospitality.
ex.ja: あなたのおもてなしにはどんなに感謝しても感謝しきれません。

note.ja: ラテン語 hospes（客・もてなす人）から。hospital（客をもてなす所 → 病院）、host、hotel も同じ。

en: A person given as a pledge or security for the performance of the conditions of a treaty or similar agreement, such as to ensure the stat…
A person seized in order to compel another party to act (or refrain from acting) in a certain way, because of the threat of harm to the h…

hostage.ety: From Middle English hostage, ostage, from Old French hostage, ostage. This, in turn, is either from Old French hoste (“host”) + -age (in which case the sense development is from taking someone into "lodging" to taking them into "captivity", to applying the term to a captive), or is from Vulgar Latin obsidāticum (“condition of being held captive”), from Latin obses (“hostage, captive”), with the initial h- added under the influence of hoste or another word. Displaced native Old English ġīsl.

ex.en: The hostages will be released before Christmas.
ex.ja: 人質はクリスマス前に解放されるだろう。

ex.en: The criminal didn't let the hostages go.
ex.ja: 犯人は人質を解放しなかった。

ex.en: Tom killed one of his hostages.
ex.ja: トムは人質のうちの１人を殺害した。

note.ja: 古フランス語 ostage（人質）から。ラテン語 obses（人質）とされるが、host（もてなす人）の影響も受けた。

en: As individuals, separately, independently.

individually.ety:
Etymology tree
English individual
Proto-Indo-European *leyg-der.
Proto-Germanic *līkąder.
Proto-Germanic *-līkaz
Proto-Germanic *-ê
Proto-Germanic *-līkê
Proto-West Germanic *-līkē
Old English -līċe
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English individually
From individual + -ly.

note.ja: individual（個人の）+ -ly。in（否定）+ dividuus（分けられる）。「それ以上分けられない」→「個々の」。divide と同じ。

en: In a manner that is impossible to avoid or prevent.
As usual; predictably; as expected.

inevitably.ety:
Etymology tree
English inevitable
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English inevitably
From inevitable + -ly.

ex.en: In addition, coincidences inevitably come in threes.
ex.ja: 偶然も３度重なれば必然になる。

ex.en: Due to his high grades, he will inevitably be accepted to the university.
ex.ja: 彼は成績がいいから必ず大学に受かるだろう。

ex.en: An oni will appear inevitably to those who fear oni.
ex.ja: 鬼を恐れている者には鬼が必ず現れる。

note.ja: in（否定）+ evitare（避ける）+ -ably。「避けられない形で」→「必然的に」。

en: A boy or young man.
A hedonistic or irresponsible young man; a Jack the lad.

lad.ety: From Middle English ladde (“foot soldier, servant; male commoner; boy”), from late Old English *ladda (attested in Old English personal byname Ladda), probably of North Germanic origin. Compare Old Norse ladd (“hose, woolen stocking; sock”), which may have undergone semantic shift to mean a term of abuse (e.g. foolish youth, youngster of lower social status, etc.); thence by connotative amelioration coming to mean any young fellow. Compare Norwegian ladd (“rough sock, woolen or felt slipper”) and the -ladd in compounds Askeladd/Askeladden (a nickname in fairy tales, "Ash Lad") and tusseladd (“

ex.en: He is as honest a lad as any.
ex.ja: 彼は誰にも負けず劣らず正直な少年だ。

ex.en: He is hardly more than a lad.
ex.ja: 彼はまだ未成年でしかない。

ex.en: The lad leaned over and shouted into Tom's ear.
ex.ja: 若者はかがみこんで、トムの耳元で大声を上げた。

note.ja: 中英語 ladde（召使いの若者）から。語源ははっきりしない。

en: The ability to read and write.
The ability to understand and evaluate something.

ex.en: Secondly, the literacy rate in Europe of that time was low.
ex.ja: 第二に、当時のヨーロッパの識字率が低かったことだ。

note.ja: literate（読み書きできる）+ -acy。ラテン語 littera（文字）。「読み書きの能力」→ 分野の「リテラシー」。

en: A migratory animal, in particular a migratory bird.
Traveller or worker who moves from one region or country to another.
Migratory.

ex.en: Migrants from the continent crossed the Japan sea.
ex.ja: 移住者は大陸から日本海を渡ってきた。

note.ja: ラテン語 migrare（移る）から。migr（移動）+ -ant。「移り住む人」→「移住者」。migrate、immigrant と同じ。

en: Deceptive or tending to mislead or create a false impression, even if technically true.
A deception that misleads.

ex.en: The latest exam was difficult and its questions misleading.
ex.ja: 今回の試験は、難しかった上に質問も紛らわしかった。

ex.en: This translation is misleading.
ex.ja: この翻訳は誤解を招く恐れがあります。

ex.en: It is not that Johnson's claim is groundless, but that it is misleading.
ex.ja: ジョンソンの主張には根拠がないということではなく、誤解を招きやすいということである。

note.ja: mis（誤って）+ lead（導く）+ -ing。「誤った方へ導く」→「誤解を招く」。

en: That which moistens or makes damp or wet; exuding fluid; liquid in small quantity.
The state of being moist.

moisture.ety: From Middle English moisture, from Old French moistour (“moisture, dampness, wetness”). Compare French moiteur.

ex.en: Rice does not like moisture. Be sure to store it well.
ex.ja: お米は湿気を嫌います。保管にはご注意ください。

ex.en: If your windows are not airtight, moisture will seep in.
ex.ja: 気密性でない窓ならば、水滴ができるだろう。

ex.en: Plant growth and productivity react sharply to a complex combination of temperature and moisture.
ex.ja: 植物の生長と生産性は、気温と湿度が作り出す入り組んだ関係に敏感に反応する。

note.ja: 古フランス語 moistour から。moist（湿った）+ -ure。「湿気・水分」。

en: A structure built for commemorative or symbolic reasons, or as a memorial; a commemoration.
An important site owned by the community as a whole.
To mark or memorialize with a monument.
To place a surveyor's monument at.

monument.ety:
From Middle English monument, from Old French monument, from Latin monumentum (“memorial, monument, tomb”), from monēre (“to remind”).
Partially displaced Old English bēacn.

ex.en: The monument was set up in the park.
ex.ja: 記念碑が公園に建てられた。

ex.en: This road will lead you to the monument.
ex.ja: この道を行けば記念碑の所へ行けますよ。

ex.en: The time spent to see the monument is short.
ex.ja: その記念碑を見るために使われる時間は短い。

note.ja: ラテン語 monumentum（思い出させるもの）から。monere（思い出させる）。「記念碑」。monitor と同系。

en: The state of being susceptible to death.
Deaths resulting from an event (such as a war, epidemic or disaster).

mortality.ety: From Old French mortalite, from Latin mortālitās, from mortālis (“relating to death”), from mors (“death”); equivalent to mortal + -ity.

ex.en: The mortality rate per 1000 live births are set out in figure 13.1.
ex.ja: 出生数１０００に対する死亡率が図１３．１に示されている。

note.ja: ラテン語 mortalitas から。mors（死）。「死ぬべき運命・死亡率」。mortal、mortgage と同じ mort。

en: The quality of being obsessed; an unshakeable feeling that one topic or activity must be pursued above other interests.
An idea that engenders a compulsive or irrational preoccupation, or the preoccupation thereby engendered.

obsession.ety: From Latin obsessio (“a besieging”), from obsidere (“to besiege”); see obsess. Equivalent to obsess + -ion.

ex.en: I can't understand his obsession with baseball.
ex.ja: なぜ彼があんなに野球に夢中になれるのか理解できない。

note.ja: ob（〜に向かって）+ sess（座る）+ ion。（悪霊が）心の前に座り込むこと →「強迫観念・執着」。

en: A legume resembling a nut, the fruit of the plant Arachis hypogaea, native to South America.
Synonym of countneck (“very small hard clam”).
To pull on somebody's tie as a prank, causing the knot to tighten.

peanut.ety: From pea + nut, perhaps a folk etymology of pinda, pinder (still found in Southern US dialects).

ex.en: Are you sure Tom isn't allergic to peanuts?
ex.ja: トムがピーナッツアレルギーじゃないって、確かなの？

ex.en: What Tom really wanted was a peanut butter sandwich.
ex.ja: トムが本当に食べたかったのは、ピーナツバターサンドだったんだ。

ex.en: If you pay peanuts, you get monkeys.
ex.ja: はした金では、良い人材は集まらない。

note.ja: pea（豆）+ nut（木の実）。「豆なのにナッツのような実」→「ピーナッツ」。

en: Obstinately refusing to give up or let go.
Insistently repetitive.

persistent.ety: From Latin persistentem, present participle of persistō (“continue steadfastly”). By surface analysis, persist + -ent.

ex.en: Be patient and persistent. These things take time.
ex.ja: 石の上にも三年、というじゃない。もう少し辛抱しなさいよ。

ex.en: She is persistent though she doesn't look so.
ex.ja: 彼女は見かけによらず頑張りやだ。

ex.en: I have a persistent pain here.
ex.ja: ここにしつこい痛みがあります。

note.ja: per（通して）+ sist（立つ）+ ent。最後まで立ち続ける →「しつこい・根気強い・持続する」。

en: A flammable liquid ranging in color from clear to very dark brown and black, consisting mainly of hydrocarbons, occurring naturally in de…

petroleum.ety: Learned borrowing from Medieval Latin petroleum. Doublet of petrol.

ex.en: Petroleum has been important since ancient times.
ex.ja: 石油は古代よりずっと重要なものであった。

ex.en: Products made from petroleum are vital to modern societies.
ex.ja: 石油製品は現代社会には欠かすことができない。

ex.en: Petroleum priced coal out of the energy market in Japan.
ex.ja: 日本では石炭が石油との価格競争に負けてエネルギー市場を失った。

note.ja: ラテン語 petra（岩）+ oleum（油）。「岩の油」→「石油」。petrol、Peter（岩）も同じ petra。

en: Of or relating to pharmacy or pharmacists.
A pharmaceutical or pharmacological preparation or product; a drug.

pharmaceutical.ety: From Latin pharmaceuticus (“of drugs”) + -al, from Ancient Greek φαρμακευτικός (pharmakeutikós, “of or by means of drugs or pharmacy”).

note.ja: ギリシャ語 pharmakeutikos（薬の）から。pharmakon（薬）。「製薬の・医薬品」。pharmacy と同じ。

en: The act of moving from one thing to another.
The act of moving forward or proceeding in a course; motion onward.

progression.ety: From Middle English progressioun, from Old French progression and its etymon Latin prōgressiō. By surface analysis, progress + -ion.

ex.en: Demo's progression was being reported by the participants through SNS.
ex.ja: デモの様子は参加者によってSNSを通じて実況された。

ex.en: Humanity is now affluent due to progression in science and technology.
ex.ja: 科学技術の進展で人類は豊かになった。

note.ja: pro（前へ）+ gress（歩む）+ ion。前へ進むこと →「進行・前進」。

en: A series of one or more shelves, stacked one above the other.
Any of various kinds of frame for holding luggage or other objects on a vehicle or vessel.
To place in or hang on a rack.
To torture (someone) on the rack.

rack.ety: From Middle English rakke, rekke, from Middle Dutch rac, recke, rec (Dutch rek), see rekken.

ex.en: That car has a roof rack.
ex.ja: その車には屋根に荷台がついています。

ex.en: Hang your coat and hat up on the rack over there.
ex.ja: 上着と帽子を向こうのラックにかけなさい。

ex.en: She was racked with pain.
ex.ja: 彼女は痛みに苦しんでいた。

note.ja: 中世オランダ語 rec（枠）から。「棚・ラック」→ 拷問台 →「苦しめる」。

en: To build again or anew.
To attempt to improve one's performance during a period of struggling.
A process or result of rebuilding.
(said of sports teams) A period during which an attempt is made to improve during a period of struggling.

rebuild.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Italic *wre-
Latin re-der.
Old French re-bor.
Middle English re-
English re-
Proto-West Germanic *buþlijan
Old English bytlan
Middle English bilden
English build
English rebuild
From re- + build.

ex.en: The castle, burnt down in 1485, was not rebuilt.
ex.ja: その城は、１４８５年に全焼して、再建されなかった。

ex.en: Our house was entirely rebuilt.
ex.ja: わが家は全面的に改築された。

note.ja: re（再び）+ build（建てる）。「建て直す」。

en: The act of rejecting.
The state of being rejected.

rejection.ety: From French réjection or directly from Latin reiectiōnem, accusative of Latin reiectiō. Displaced native Old English āworpennes (literally “thrown-out-ness”).

note.ja: re（後ろへ）+ jacere（投げる）+ -ion。「投げ返すこと」→「拒絶」。reject、project と同じ ject。

en: A place where anything is kept in store.
A large natural or artificial lake used as a source of water supply.
To store or keep (something) in or as in a reservoir.

reservoir.ety: From French réservoir (“collection place”) (fig.), réservoir (“storehouse”) (lit.). in turn from French réserver (“to reserve, keep”).

ex.en: There's a reservoir near where I live.
ex.ja: 住んでるところの近くにため池があるんだ。

ex.en: Near where I live is a reservoir.
ex.ja: 住んでるところの近くにため池があるんだ。

ex.en: There is a reservoir near my house.
ex.ja: 家の近くに貯水池があります。

note.ja: re（後ろに）+ serv（保つ）+ oir。後ろに取っておく場所 →「貯水池・蓄え」。

en: A (small) piece; a fragment; a detached, incomplete portion.
The smallest amount.
To discard; to get rid of.
To stop working on (a project or plan) indefinitely.

scrap.ety: From Middle English scrappe, from Old Norse skrap, from skrapa (“to scrape, scratch”), from Proto-Germanic *skrapōną, *skrepaną (“to scrape, scratch”), from Proto-Indo-European *skreb-, *skrep- (“to engrave”). Cf. Swedish skräp (“garbage”).

ex.en: There wasn't a scrap of truth in the statement.
ex.ja: その声明には真実のかけらもなかった。

ex.en: This car will soon have to go for scrap.
ex.ja: この車はもうすぐスクラップだ。

ex.en: Please get me a scrap of paper.
ex.ja: 紙切れを取ってきてください。

note.ja: 北欧語 skrap（くず）から。scrape（こする）と同系。「削りくず」→「切れ端・廃棄する」。

en: A physical feeling or perception from something that comes into contact with the body; something sensed.
Excitation of sensory organs.

sensation.ety: From Old French, from Medieval Latin sensatio, from Latin sensus.

ex.en: I felt a burning sensation all over.
ex.ja: 全身が焼き尽くされるような感じがした。

ex.en: The movie created a great sensation.
ex.ja: その映画は一大センセーションを巻き起こした。

ex.en: The news caused a great sensation.
ex.ja: そのニュースは大評判を巻き起こした。

note.ja: sens（感じる）+ ation。感じること →「感覚・大評判」。

en: The long, narrow, central body of a spear, arrow, or javelin.
Anything cast or thrown as a spear or javelin.
To equip with a shaft.

shaft.ety:
From Middle English chafte, saft, scaft, schaft, schafte, scheft, shaffet, shaft, from Old English sċeaft, from Proto-West Germanic *skaft, from Proto-Germanic *skaftaz (“shaft”), from Proto-Indo-European *skeh₂p- (“club, rod, shaft, staff”).
Cognates
Cognate with Dutch schacht (“shaft”), German Schaft (“shaft”), Low German Schacht, Skacht (“shaft; cane, stick; beating”), Danish, Icelandic, Norwegian Bokmål, Norwegian Nynorsk, and Swedish skaft (“handle; stem; shaft”); also Latin scapus (“stalk, stem; shaft”), Greek σκήπτρο (skíptro, “sceptre”), Albanian shkop (“staff, stick”), Belarusian кап'

ex.en: From here, you can look down the elevator shaft.
ex.ja: ここから、エレベーターシャフトを見下ろせます。

ex.en: This shaft links with a piston.
ex.ja: このシャフトはピストンとつながっている。

note.ja: 古英語 sceaft（槍の柄）から。「柄・軸」→ 細長い穴 →「縦穴」、光の筋。

en: A person who tends sheep, especially a grazing flock.
A male sheep tender
To watch over; to guide.
To obstruct an opponent from getting to the ball, either when a teammate has it or is going for it, or if the ball is about to bounce thr…

shepherd.ety: From Middle English schepherde, from Old English sċēaphierde, a compound of sċēap (“sheep”) and hierde (“herdsman”), equivalent to modern sheep + herd (“herder”).

ex.en: The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.
ex.ja: ヱホバは我が牧者なり　われ乏しきことあらじ

ex.en: The Lord is my shepherd, I shall not want.
ex.ja: 主はわたしの牧者であって、わたしには乏しいことがない。

ex.en: The German Shepherd was limping down the street.
ex.ja: そのシェパードは、びっこをひきながら道を歩いていた。

note.ja: sheep（羊）+ herd（群れの番人）。「羊の番人」→「羊飼い」。

en: A tool used to carry the woof back and forth between the warp threads on a loom.
The sliding thread holder in a sewing machine, which carries the lower thread through a loop of the upper thread, to make a lock stitch.
To go or send back and forth between two places.
To transport by shuttle or by means of a shuttle service.

shuttle.ety:
From a merger of two words:
* Middle English shutel, shotel, schetel, schettell, schyttyl, scutel (“bar; bolt”), from Old English sċyttel, sċutel (“bar; bolt”), equivalent to shut + -le
* Middle English shutel, schetil, shotil, shetel, schootyll, shutyll, schytle, scytyl (“missile; projectile; spear”), from Old English sċytel, sċutel (“dart, arrow”), from Proto-Germanic *skutilaz.
The name for a loom weaving instrument, recorded from 1338, is from a sense of being "shot" across the threads. The back-and-forth imagery inspired the extension to "passenger trains" in 1895, aircraft in 1942, and s

ex.en: Where should I wait for the shuttle bus?
ex.ja: リムジンはどこで待てばいいのですか。

ex.en: Where can I find a shuttle bus?
ex.ja: リムジンはどこですか。

ex.en: My dream is to travel in a space shuttle.
ex.ja: 私の夢はスペースシャトルで旅することです。

note.ja: 古英語 scytel（投げ矢）から。shoot（撃つ）と同じ祖先。織機で左右に飛ばす「杼（ひ）」→「往復便」。※ 綴りや別語義（かんぬき）では shut（閉じる）由来の語とも合流している。

en: A surface that either inclines or declines in a regular manner from the perspective of an observer.
An area of ground that tends evenly upward or downward.
To tend steadily upward or downward.
To form with a slope; to give an oblique or slanting direction to; to incline or slant.

ex.en: We had to go up and down the slopes.
ex.ja: 私たちは坂を上がったり下がったりしなければならなかった。

ex.en: I went down the slope, falling again and again.
ex.ja: 私は何度も転びながら、坂を下っていった。

ex.en: In old times the slope was very lonely.
ex.ja: 昔はその坂はとてもさびしかった。

note.ja: aslope（斜めに）の短縮。slip（すべる）と同系とされる。「坂・斜面」。

en: A light meal.
An item of food eaten between meals.
To eat a light meal.
To eat between meals.

snack.ety: From Middle Dutch snacken (“to snack”), possibly from Proto-Germanic *snakkōną (“to smack one's lips, open one's mouth to eat; to snatch (with one's mouth?), snack on”), whence also etymology 2; ultimately onomatopoeic. Cognate with German schnäken (“to snack”). More at Proto-Germanic *snak-.

ex.en: Do we have anything I can snack on?
ex.ja: 何かおつまみない？

ex.en: Tom, you just had a snack right now.
ex.ja: トム、今つまみ食いしたでしょ。

ex.en: There's enough time for a quick snack.
ex.ja: 急いで食事をするだけの時間はある。

note.ja: 中世オランダ語 snacken（かみつく）から。「ぱくっと食べるもの」→「軽食」。

en: A bright, directional light or lamp, especially one used to illuminate the focus or center of attention on a stage.
The circle of light shed by a spotlight.
To illuminate with a spotlight.
To draw attention to.

ex.en: We will put up spotlights.
ex.ja: スポットライトを取り付けます。

ex.en: We'll put up spotlights.
ex.ja: スポットライトを取り付けます。

note.ja: spot（点）+ light（光）。「一点を照らす光」→「スポットライト・注目」。

en: An act of stabbing or thrusting with an object to hurt or kill someone.
A wound made by stabbing.
To pierce or to wound (somebody) with a (usually pointed) tool or weapon, especially a knife or dagger.
To thrust in a stabbing motion.

stab.ety:
First attested in Scottish English (compare Scots stob, stobbe, stabb (“a pointed stick or stake; a thrust with a pointed weapon”)), from Middle English stabbe (“a stab”), probably a variant of Middle English stob, stub, stubbe (“pointed stick, stake, thorn, stub, stump”), from Old Norse stobbi, stubbi, cognate with Old English stybb. Cognate with Middle Dutch stobbe.
Supposed by some to derive from Scottish Gaelic stob (“to prick, to prod, to push, to thrust”); supposed by others to be from a Scots word.

ex.en: Here, let me take a stab at it.
ex.ja: ほら、俺にもやらせてくれ。

ex.en: He stabbed me in the back!
ex.ja: やつは僕を裏切ったんだ！

ex.en: She stabbed him in the back.
ex.ja: 彼女は彼の背中を刺した。

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。stub（切り株）と関係するとされる。「突き刺す」。

en: Having a hardness and severity of nature or manner.
Grim and forbidding in appearance.
The rear part (after end) of a ship or other vessel.
The post of management or direction.
To propel or move backward or stern-first in the water.

stern.ety: From Middle English stern, sterne, sturne, from Old English styrne (“stern, grave, strict, austere, hard, severe, cruel”), from Proto-Germanic *sturnijaz (“angry, astonished, shocked”), from Proto-Indo-European *ster- (“rigid, stiff”). Cognate with Scots stern (“bold, courageous, fierce, resolute”), Old High German stornēn (“to be astonished”), Dutch stuurs (“glum, austere”), Swedish stursk (“insolent”).

ex.en: He looks stern, but actually he's very kind.
ex.ja: 彼は厳しそうに見えるが実際はとても親切だ。

ex.en: Her stern look got him to quit talking.
ex.ja: 彼女は怖い顔をして彼を黙らせた。

ex.en: I gave him a stern talking-to.
ex.ja: こってりあいつの油を絞ってやった。

note.ja: 「厳しい」は古英語 styrne から。「船尾」は北欧語 stjórn（かじ取り）からで別語。steer と同系。

en: Rigid; hard to bend; inflexible.
Inflexible; rigid.
Any hard hand where it is possible to exceed 21 by drawing an additional card.
To fail to pay that which one owes (implicitly or explicitly) to another, especially by departing hastily.
To cheat someone.
Of the wind, with great force; strongly.

stiff.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *steyp
Proto-Germanic *stīfaz
Proto-West Germanic *stīf
Old English stīf
Middle English stif
English stiff
From Middle English stiff, stiffe, stif, from Old English stīf, from Proto-West Germanic *stīf, from Proto-Germanic *stīfaz, from Proto-Indo-European *steypós.
See also West Frisian stiif, Dutch stijf, Norwegian Bokmål stiv, German steif; also Latin stīpes, stīpō, from which English stevedore.
The expected Modern English form would be /staɪf/; /stɪf/ is probably originally from compounds such as stiffly, where the vowel was shortened before a consonant c

ex.en: Shoes are stiff when they are new.
ex.ja: 靴は新しい間は硬い。

ex.en: I walked till my legs got stiff.
ex.ja: 足が棒になるまで歩いた。

ex.en: I have a bad stiff neck.
ex.ja: 肩こりがひどいのです。

note.ja: 古英語 stīf（硬い）から。「こわばった」→（肩などが）凝った。

en: A person who is on strike, someone who has stopped working as a protest.
A blacksmith's assistant who wields the sledgehammer.

striker.ety:
Etymology tree
English strike
Proto-Indo-European *-eh₂
Proto-Indo-European *-os?
Proto-Indo-European *-o-
Proto-Indo-European *-so-
Proto-Indo-European *-eh₂so-
Proto-Indo-European *-yós
Proto-Indo-European *-eh₂s(i)yós

From strike + -er.

ex.en: The strikers called off the strike of their own accord.
ex.ja: ストライキをしていた労働者達は、自らストライキを中止した。

note.ja: strike（打つ）+ -er。「打つ人」→「点取り屋」。

en: Very strong or intense; excessive, tremendous.
Extremely good; excellent, amazing.

terrific.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *tres-
Proto-Indo-European *-yeti
Proto-Indo-European *-éyeti
Proto-Indo-European *troséyeti
Proto-Italic *troseō
Latin terreō
Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁-der.
Proto-Italic *θakos
Proto-Italic *-fakos
Latin -ficus
Latin terrificusder.
French terrifiqueder.
English terrific
From French terrifique, and its source, Latin terrificus (“terrifying”), from terrēre (“to frighten, terrify”) + -ficus, related to facere (“to make”). By surface analysis, terrify + -ic.
The sense of excellent or amazing is an ameliorative semantic shift from the original sense of terrifyin

ex.en: A car went by at terrific speed.
ex.ja: 車が猛スピードで通り過ぎていった。

ex.en: The performance received terrific applause from the audience.
ex.ja: その演奏は聴衆からすばらしい拍手を得た。

ex.en: He came up with a terrific solution to the complex problem.
ex.ja: 彼はその複雑な問題を解決するすばらしい方法を思いついた。

note.ja: ラテン語 terrificus（怖がらせる）から。terror と同じ。もとは「恐ろしい」→「ものすごい」→「すばらしい」と意味が良くなった。

en: Something or someone of very large stature, greatness, or godliness.

note.ja: ギリシャ神話の巨人族ティーターン（Titans）から。titanic（巨大な）。

en: A widely cultivated plant, Solanum lycopersicum, having edible fruit.
The savory fruit of this plant, most often red when ripe, treated as a vegetable in horticulture and cooking.
Of a shade of red, the colour of a ripe tomato.

tomato.ety: Variant of earlier tomate, from Spanish tomate, from Classical Nahuatl tomatl, from Proto-Nahuan *toma-tl. Compare tomatillo.

ex.en: I don't want to eat just tomatoes anymore.
ex.ja: トマトばかり食べるのはもういやだ。

ex.en: I don't want to eat only tomatoes anymore.
ex.ja: トマトばかり食べるのはもういやだ。

ex.en: The tomato is subject to a number of diseases.
ex.ja: トマトは多くの病気にかかりやすい。

note.ja: ナワトル語（アステカの言語）tomatl からスペイン語を経た語。

en: The quality of being transparent.
Openness; accessibility to scrutiny.

transparency.ety: Borrowed from Medieval Latin trānspārentia, equivalent to transparent + -cy.

note.ja: trans（通して）+ pare（見える）+ ncy。向こうが透けて見えること →「透明性・透明度」。

en: A group or set of three people or things; three things combined into one.
The state of being three; independence of three things; things divided into three.

trinity.ety: From Middle English trinite, from Anglo-Norman trinite and Old French ternite (modern French trinité), from Latin trīnitās, from trīnī (“three each”), from trēs (“three”). By surface analysis, trine + -ity. Displaced native Old English þrines (literally “threeness”).

note.ja: ラテン語 trinitas（3つ組）から。trinus（3つずつ）。tri（3）と同じ。

en: Having no job despite being able and willing to work.
Having no use, not doing work
The unemployed people of a society or the world, taken collectively.

unemployed.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *né
Proto-Indo-European *n̥-
Proto-Germanic *un-
Proto-West Germanic *un-
Old English un-
Middle English un-
English un-
English employed
English unemployed
From un- + employed.

ex.en: The number of unemployed people will rise by degrees.
ex.ja: 失業者数は徐々に増加するだろう。

ex.en: Many young people in Spain are unemployed.
ex.ja: スペインでは多くの若者が失業している。

ex.en: I think that Tom is still unemployed.
ex.ja: トムはまだプータローしてるんだと思うよ。

note.ja: un（否定）+ employ（雇う）+ -ed。employ は im（中に）+ plicare（折る）。「中に組み込む」→「雇う」。

en: To undo or open a lock or something locked by, for example, turning a key, or selecting a combination.
To obtain access to something; to meet the requirements of a security or protection system.
The act of unlocking something.
An initially hidden feature that is made available to reward the player for some achievement.

unlock.ety: From Middle English unloken, unlouken, onlouken, from Old English onlūcan (“to unlock”), equivalent to un- + lock. Cognate with Dutch ontluiken (“to unlock”).

ex.en: To my surprise, the door was unlocked.
ex.ja: 驚いたことにドアの錠がはずされていた。

ex.en: She was careful not to leave the door unlocked.
ex.ja: 玄関のかぎをかけわすれないように気をつけた。

ex.en: She had left the front door unlocked.
ex.ja: 彼女は玄関の鍵をかけないままにしていた。

note.ja: un（逆に）+ lock（鍵をかける）。「鍵を開ける」→ 能力などを「引き出す」。

en: An arched masonry structure supporting and forming a ceiling, whether freestanding or forming part of a larger building.
Any arched ceiling or roof.
To build as, or cover with a vault.
To store in a vault.

vault.ety: From Middle English vaute, vowte, from Old French volte (modern voûte), from Vulgar Latin *volta < *volvita or *volŭta, a regularization of Latin volūta (compare modern volute (“spire”)), the past participle of volvere (“roll, turn”). Cognate with Spanish vuelta (“turn”) and Portuguese volta ("turn"). Doublet of volute. Displaced native Old English hwealf.

note.ja: 「金庫室・丸天井」はラテン語 volvere（転がす・曲げる）から、アーチ状の天井。「跳躍」はイタリア語 voltare（向きを変える）から。どちらも volv（回る）系。

en: A veterinarian or veterinary surgeon.
To thoroughly check or investigate particularly with regard to providing formal approval.

ex.en: My brother is a vet.
ex.ja: 兄は獣医なんです。

ex.en: As a child, Tom dreamt of becoming a vet.
ex.ja: トムは子どもの頃、獣医になるのが夢だった。

ex.en: As a kid, Tom dreamt of being a vet.
ex.ja: トムは子どもの頃、獣医になるのが夢だった。

note.ja: veterinarian（獣医）と veteran（退役軍人）の短縮。別々の語。「獣医が動物を診る」→「綿密に調べる」。

en: A heavier four-wheeled (normally horse-drawn) vehicle designed to carry goods (or sometimes people).
A shopping cart.
To load into a wagon in preparation for transportation; to transport by means of a wagon.

ex.ja: インドネシア語ができますか。

ex.en: The Indonesian sentence is a perfect side by side translation of its English counterpart.
ex.ja: インドネシア語の文は英文の対訳としては完璧です。

note.ja: Indonesia（インドの島々）+ -ian。ギリシャ語 nēsos（島）、Polynesia（多くの島々）と同じ。

en: A person that leases real property; a lessor.
The owner or manager of a public house.

landlord.ety: From Middle English londlord, landlorde, from Old English landhlāford, equivalent to land + lord. Cognate with Scots landlaird, Middle Low German lantlord (“homeowner, landlord”).

ex.en: The landlord used to be quite well off.
ex.ja: その地主は以前かなり裕福な暮らしをしていた。

ex.en: They say the landlord used to be well off.
ex.ja: その大家は以前は暮らし向きがよかったそうだ。

ex.en: The landlord says he wants to raise the rent.
ex.ja: 大家さんは家賃をあげたいそうだ。

note.ja: land（土地）+ lord（主人）。「土地の主」→「家主・地主」。

en: An object that marks the boundary of a piece of land (usually a stone, or a tree).
A recognizable natural or man-made feature used for navigation.
To officially designate a site or building as a landmark.

landmark.ety: From Middle English *landmark, from Old English landmearc (“boundary”), from Proto-West Germanic *landamarku (“boundary, landmark”). Equivalent to land + mark. Cognate with German Landmarke (“landmark”), Danish landemærke (“landmark”), Swedish landmärke (“landmark”), Norwegian landemerke (“landmark”) and Faroese landamark (“land frontier”). Compare also Middle English londes-mark (“boundary”).

ex.en: You can get in touch with me at Hotel Landmark.
ex.ja: ランドマークホテルに連絡してくれれば、大丈夫だ。

ex.en: Are there any landmarks?
ex.ja: 何か目印がありますか。

ex.en: I wish to know a landmark nearby so I can find my way there.
ex.ja: そこに行く道がわかるように、近くの目印を教えて下さい。

note.ja: land（土地）+ mark（印）。「土地の境界の印」→「目印・名所」→「画期的な出来事」。

en: Bound or obliged in law or equity; responsible; answerable.
Subject; susceptible; prone.

liable.ety:
From Old French lier (“to bind”), from Latin ligō, ligāre (“to bind, to tie”).
Compare typologically Russian обя́занный (objázannyj), обяза́тельный (objazátelʹnyj) (akin to вяза́ть (vjazátʹ)).

ex.en: My wife is liable to catch a cold.
ex.ja: 妻は風邪を引きやすい。

ex.en: In a similar situation, the company was held liable.
ex.ja: よく似たケースで責任は会社にあるとされた。

ex.en: We are all liable to make mistakes.
ex.ja: 人はだれでも誤りを犯しやすい。

note.ja: 古フランス語 lier（縛る）から。ラテン語 ligare。「縛られた」→「責任がある・〜しがちな」。liability と同じ。
